articles.title: Houston’s long-vacant Greenspoint Mall is set to be demolished next month; the former regional shopping center will make way for an 80-acre redevelopment featuring a $150 million industrial park with 1.2 million square feet
articles.summary: For years, the largely vacant Greenspoint Mall has stood as a reminder of how dramatically Houston’s retail landscape has changed.
articles.body: For years, the largely vacant Greenspoint Mall has stood as a reminder of how dramatically Houston’s retail landscape has changed. Now, the former North Houston shopping centre is headed for demolition, with a much different future planned for the property. Lincoln Property Company, in partnership with New York Life Investment Management, announced plans for CityNorth Industrial Park, a $150 million redevelopment covering approximately 80 acres. According to Lincoln’s announcement, the project will replace the former mall with 1.2 million square feet of industrial buildings, along with retail and service uses. Demolition is expected to begin in October 2026.From a major shopping destination to a vacant propertyGreenspoint Mall once occupied an important place in North Houston’s retail scene. The mall opened in the 1970s and operated for nearly five decades, but its fortunes changed as shopping habits shifted and competition from newer retail destinations increased. The property eventually became largely vacant, and the main mall closed in 2024. The Houston Chronicle reported that the site had gone through years of decline and unsuccessful attempts at revitalisation before its closure.That long period of vacancy is now approaching its final chapter. Lincoln and New York Life Investment Management have acquired the approximately 80-acre mall site and are planning to clear the existing structure for a new commercial development. The redevelopment is planned at 12300 North Freeway, near the northeast corner of Interstate 45 and Beltway 8. The location also has access to the Hardy Toll Road, putting the future industrial park close to several major transportation routes.A $150 million industrial park will replace the mallThe planned CityNorth Industrial Park will be significantly different from the enclosed shopping centre that previously occupied the property. The $150 million project is expected to deliver approximately 1.2 million square feet of industrial space in a combination of cross-dock and rear-load buildings. The development will also include retail and service uses, creating a mix of commercial activity rather than simply replacing the mall with another retail centre.The industrial buildings are intended to serve logistics and distribution companies, as well as smaller businesses looking for space in North Houston. Lincoln said the size of the property gives the project flexibility to accommodate different types of users. The location is an important part of the redevelopment strategy. With Interstate 45, Beltway 8 and the Hardy Toll Road nearby, the site has direct connections to major parts of the Houston area. The developers say those transportation links will help CityNorth serve the region’s logistics and industrial demand.Demolition begins in OctoberThe first visible step in the transformation is expected to begin next month. According to Lincoln, demolition of the former mall is scheduled to start in October 2026. Construction will then move towards the first phase of CityNorth Industrial Park, which is currently scheduled for completion in the first quarter of 2028. The developers have not yet announced all of the future tenants or released every detail of the building-by-building leasing plan.The project is expected to generate employment during construction as well as after the industrial park is completed. According to Lincoln, the development could support approximately 300 construction jobs and accommodate about 1,200 full-time jobs once the property is fully developed and leased. Fitness Connection, which currently operates at the former mall property, is also expected to remain. As part of the redevelopment, the gym is planned to move into a new 45,500-square-foot build-to-suit facility at CityNorth.Part of wider Greenspoint redevelopmentThe transformation of the former mall site is also taking place alongside broader efforts to revive the surrounding Greenspoint area. The city of Houston established the Greater Greenspoint Tax Increment Reinvestment Zone (TIRZ) to support infrastructure, mobility and other public improvements intended to encourage redevelopment in the area. Lincoln said it is working with the city and the North Houston District as plans for CityNorth move forward. The city’s reinvestment zone is expected to provide funding toward the redevelopment, although details of the funding were not immediately clear.For a property associated with years of declining retail activity and vacancy, the planned industrial park represents a substantial change in how the site will be used. Instead of attempting to restore the former shopping centre, the new owners are positioning the property around industrial, logistics and employment uses. If the current schedule holds, the first phase of CityNorth Industrial Park will be completed in early 2028. By then, the former Greenspoint Mall will have given way to a large industrial development designed around the transportation network and commercial needs of North Houston.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: Watch: UK police robot targets vans near airbase used by US forces
articles.summary: A bomb-disposal robot was deployed around three suspicious vans near RAF Fairford, a British air base used by US bombers, after Gloucestershire Police
articles.body: A bomb-disposal robot was deployed around three suspicious vans near RAF Fairford, a British air base used by US bombers, after Gloucestershire Police arrested five men who were later held on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act.A video shared on X appeared to show the remotely operated machine moving around the vehicles near the Gloucestershire airfield. Aerial footage showed two vans with their rear doors open and large dark objects nearby, while the robot appeared to be trying to gain access to the third vehicle.Gloucestershire Police received a call at about 12.45am on Sunday about three suspicious vehicles apparently travelling towards RAF Fairford. Armed officers arrested five men in Whelford on suspicion of offences under the Explosives Act. They were subsequently arrested on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act, with Counter Terrorism Policing taking over the investigation.Police imposed a 400-metre cordon around the vehicles while the Army's explosive ordnance disposal unit examined them. About 85 households were evacuated as a precaution. Gloucestershire Police said the immediate incident appeared to be contained.Police have not announced a motive. Reuters reported that investigators were giving greatest weight to a possible Iran link, while also examining whether Russian sabotage or an Islamist plot was involved, citing a person familiar with the inquiry.The five men remained in custody on Monday as police questioned them. Their nationalities have not been disclosed. Defence minister Wes Streeting said he would not speculate about the motive while the investigation was ongoing.Trump says suspects were ‘looking to do big damage’The US president, Donald Trump, said the suspects had been “looking to do big damage”.“We had them under view for a long time, and we got them,” Trump told reporters in Chicago. He said British and American authorities had been investigating the men before their arrests.A local farmer told the Daily Telegraph she alerted police after encountering the vans and seeing several men, some with their faces covered, moving towards nearby fields.RAF Fairford hosts the headquarters of the US Air Force's 501st Combat Support Wing and the 420th Air Base Squadron. Britain had authorised US bombers based there to strike Iranian missile sites that were attacking shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.In July, Iran's Revolutionary Guards warned Britain against allowing US bombers to fly from Fairford, saying bases used to launch attacks could be treated as legitimate targets. Tehran has previously rejected claims that it was behind attacks or plots in the UK or other countries.Security was tightened around Fairford following the arrests. Measures were also increased at RAF Lakenheath and RAF Mildenhall, two other British bases used by US forces.Vicki Evans, senior national coordinator for Counter Terrorism Policing, said officers were still gathering evidence and establishing the circumstances of the incident. Under the Terrorism Act 2000, the five men can be detained for up to 14 days without charge.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 'We call it kidnapping': CJP's Ashutosh Ranka calls Assam Police action completely illegal
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka, who was detained along with several party leaders alleged on Monday that the Assam
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka, who was detained along with several party leaders alleged on Monday that the Assam Police action was "completely illegal."Ranka, who was later released, alleged that CJP members were picked up from private property without being informed of the grounds for their detention.Ranka alleged that the police failed to provide a specific reason for the action. “It wasn't a detention. It was completely illegal because they picked us up from private property. We don't call this detention; we call it kidnapping,” he said.“When we asked the police on what grounds we were detained, their only reply was, 'Sir, we have orders from above, so we arrested you, detained you.' And even after that, when we continuously asked while we were there, they couldn't give us any other reason,” Ranka alleged.He also accused Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma of attempting to suppress the organisation's activities.“The government's intention was to bully us. Hemanta Biswa Sarma wanted to intimidate us, but Hemanta Biswa Sarma made the same mistake that Amit Shah made on July 20th. The more you suppress, the more the revolution will spread,” he said.“Now, Assam CJP will see how students and youth issues will be raised in the coming times,” Ranka added.Ranka said CJP plans to expand its activities across Assam and other Northeastern states, focusing on issues concerning students and young people.“There are many issues in Assam; there are a lot of local issues here. The condition of schools here is very poor, especially in the remote areas where most schools don't even have their own buildings,” he said.“A complete facade has been created in the name of development, but we want the country to see the reality of that development,” Ranka added. He said the organisation would also raise issues related to floods, Kaziranga and other local concerns.“All the student and youth-centric issues that the youth of Assam have been struggling with for a long time, we will work on all of them in the coming time. We will definitely go to other Northeast states. We have received a very good response, a very good support,” Ranka said.The CJP leaders were detained on Sunday shortly before the organisation's first regional volunteers' meeting in Guwahati was scheduled to begin near the Assam Secretariat.The organisation said several senior leaders and Assam-based volunteers, including Ranka, Ankit Bhardwaj and Prem Aakash, were taken to a police facility. Reports said around 30 CJP workers were detained.The CJP had described the gathering as a peaceful meeting on private property. Assam Police has not publicly provided a detailed explanation for the detentions, according to the information available.CJP to begin nationwide protest from Oct 2Ranka also said that CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke had initially planned to travel to Assam following the detentions but would now focus on preparations for the organisation's proposed October 2 protest over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and its demand for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.“Abhijit's plan was based on our arrest yesterday. But as I've been released, Abhijit is not coming. He is busy preparing for the protest planned for October 2nd regarding SIR and Gyanesh Kumar's resignation,” Ranka told reporters.On the demand for Kumar's resignation, Ranka said the organisation would launch a nationwide protest from October 2.“It will happen now. For 48 hours, the ball was in Gyanesh Kumar's court. Now the ball is in CJP's court. We'll start our nationwide protest from 2nd October, and we won't back down until Ganeshkumar resigns,” he added.Ranka also alleged that more than 13 crore people had been removed from electoral rolls and questioned the process of electoral boundary redrawing in Assam. These claims were made by Ranka and CJP and have not been independently established.The remarks come amid a wider political dispute over the functioning of the Election Commission and the SIR exercise. An Indian Express report cited by CJP said Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections on multiple occasions over SIR-related decisions.The Election Commission has rejected allegations of internal disagreement and maintained that decisions concerning SIR were taken with the “unanimous approval of the Commission.” The detentions came after the leadership of Akhil Gogoi-led Raijor Dal met CJP leaders, including Ranka, in Guwahati.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Leave us alone': 3 female LPU students allege university posted video without consent
articles.summary: PHAGWARA: Three female students of Lovely Professional University (LPU) on Monday said the university did not take their consent before posting a video in
articles.body: PHAGWARA: Three female students of Lovely Professional University (LPU) on Monday said the university did not take their consent before posting a video in which they appeared to dismiss claims of a student's rape on campus, and said they were now facing abuse and harassment.The students also claimed that the video released by the university had been cropped.The development came a day after LPU released the video featuring the three students in an attempt to pacify protests that had erupted on campus over claims that a female student was raped by a plumber three days earlier.On Monday, the three students posted a video on social media objecting to the university's use of their earlier recording."Our video has been trimmed and posted on Instagram. We had no idea about this, and no consent was taken from us. Now, unnecessarily, we are being abused," one of the students said in the clip circulating on social media."We have no role, please leave us alone," another student said.What LPU had posted earlierThe LPU management had maintained that there was no truth in the rape rumours. Registrar Dr Monica Gulati on Sunday said some anti-social elements were spreading "false, baseless and fabricated" allegations.The university subsequently released a video of more than a minute featuring Gulati's statement followed by comments from the three female students from Room No. 504 of the hostel.In the video, one of the students said, "We are students of room number 504 and nothing of the sort has happened in our room. We have been living in the room for the past two months. Please, students and police should not come to harass us."Another student said they would involve their parents if they were troubled, while the third said, "And police should not come to our room repeatedly; otherwise, we will call our parents".At the end of the video, Gulati said the conclusion to be drawn was that "anti-social elements and individuals with vested interests" were behind the allegations. "It is a conspiracy to tarnish the university's reputation through false and fabricated rumours." LPU protest, highway blockadeThe protest began near Girls' Hostel-3 around 1am on Sunday and later escalated, with students vandalising property and blocking a stretch of the New Delhi-Amritsar Highway outside the campus.Traffic movement on National Highway-44 in Phagwara, which had remained blocked by the students for more than 15 hours, was restored on Monday, police said.The situation has also been brought under control.The students' protest had followed claims that a female student staying on the campus had been raped.Police registered a case on the students' complaint and formed a special investigation team to probe the allegations.(With PTI inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chandigarh | Silver Rate in Chandigarh | Bank Holidays in Chandigarh | Public Holidays in Chandigarh | Chandigarh AQI | Weather in Chandigarh | Petrol Price in Chandigarh | Diesel Price in Chandigarh | CNG Price in Chandigarh | LPG Price in ChandigarhStay updated with the latest Chandigarh news. articles.title: In 2006, Muhammad Ali, Mia Hamm and other elite athletes founded Athletes for Hope to help fellow athletes give back
articles.summary: In 2006, a group of elite athletes who had given their time, energy, and resources to charitable causes began a conversation that led to Athletes for Hope.
articles.body: In 2006, a group of elite athletes who had given their time, energy, and resources to charitable causes began a conversation that led to Athletes for Hope. Boxer Muhammad Ali was among them. They noticed that many of their fellow athletes wanted to make a difference in the world but did not know where to begin. Their answer was a new charity built to remove the barriers to giving back and to bring every nonprofit-inspired athlete together around a common goal. Its founding athletes page profiles seven members, from Muhammad Ali and Mia Hamm to Andre Agassi, Alonzo Mourning, and Jeff Gordon.Why the elite athletes founded ‘Athletes for Hope’The idea for Athletes for Hope grew out of a dialogue in 2006 among elite athletes who were already deeply committed to charitable causes, giving generously of their time, energy, and resources. According to the Athletes for Hope Organisation, what they noticed was a gap, plenty of other athletes felt the same pull to make a positive difference in the world, yet had no idea where to start. Instead of leaving that gap in place, the group founded Athletes for Hope with a clear aim. The organisation would eliminate the barriers that keep athletes from giving back and bring every nonprofit-inspired athlete together around one common goal, making a difference in the world.Muhammad Ali, the boxer whose greatest triumphs came outside the ringMuhammad Ali leads the list of founding athletes. The organisation describes him as a boxer with an unorthodox fighting style, unprecedented speed, and extraordinary grace, whose charm and wit changed what the public expected of a champion. Yet it says his greatest triumphs came outside the ring, through humanitarian work that perhaps did more than any other athlete's to make the world a better place. He received the 1997 Arthur Ashe Courage Award and the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2005. Ali passed away in 2016, and his legacy lives on through the Muhammad Ali Center in his birthplace of Louisville, Kentucky, where children and adults learn and form new commitments to personal growth, integrity, and respect for others.How Mia Hamm and Warrick Dunn built charities that support families in needSeveral founding athletes built their own charities before Athletes for Hope existed. Mia Hamm, who won two Olympic gold medals, one Olympic silver medal, and two World Cups, started the Mia Hamm Foundation in 1999, two years after her brother Garrett died from complications of a rare blood disorder. It raises funds and awareness for families needing marrow or cord blood transplants and promotes programs for young women in sports. Its all-star exhibition soccer matches bring marrow recipients together with their donors at halftime for the first time. Warrick Dunn, a former running back and Pro Bowl player, founded Homes For The Holidays in 1997, his rookie season with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, inspired by his mother Betty's dream of owning a home. The program provides home furnishings and down-payment assistance to single-parent families.Andre Agassi, Jackie Joyner-Kersee, Alonzo Mourning, and Jeff Gordon focused on young peopleThe remaining founders on the page share a focus on children and youth. Andre Agassi's foundation partnered with the Clark County School District in Las Vegas to open the Andre Agassi College Preparatory Academy in 2001, a public charter school whose first graduating class had a 100 per cent college acceptance rate. Jackie Joyner-Kersee, a six-time Olympic medalist, created the Jackie Joyner-Kersee Center and a foundation that aims to give every young person in her home area the chance to succeed in academics, athletics, and leadership. Alonzo Mourning and his wife, Tracy, have raised more than $25 million through the Mourning Family Foundation, founded in 1997, for youth programs in South Florida, and he delivers turkey dinners to hundreds of families every Thanksgiving. Jeff Gordon's children's foundation has granted millions to children's charities, a commitment that began after his crew chief's son was diagnosed with leukaemia in 1992.You use AI every day. articles.title: US Navy has approved terms for redevelopment of 2,422 acres at California’s former Concord Naval Weapons Station; the master developer will pay $44.6 million plus interest as the abandoned military site moves toward a new future
articles.summary: The US Navy has approved an agreement that clears the way for the redevelopment of about 2,422 acres at the former Concord Naval Weapons Station in
articles.body: The US Navy has approved an agreement that clears the way for the redevelopment of about 2,422 acres at the former Concord Naval Weapons Station in California. The agreement allows the City of Concord and master developer Brookfield Properties to move ahead with plans for the former military site, SFGATE reported Friday.The naval weapons station opened in 1944 as a munitions storage facility and fell out of use in 1999. Although Concord officially marked the property for redevelopment in 2006, the wider 12,800-acre site has remained undeveloped for about two decades.The newly approved Term Sheet sets the financial terms for the transfer of about 2,422 acres from the US Navy. Concord is the federally recognised local redevelopment authority for the former weapons station, while Brookfield is the project's master developer.Under the agreement, Brookfield will pay $44.6 million for the property, along with interest on part of the amount. The deal includes an initial payment of $4.6 million, followed by $40 million in deferred payments over four years.What happens nextThe Navy's approval means the project can now move into its next stage. Concord and Brookfield will begin preparing a Specific Plan that will lay out how the area could be developed, including its layout, uses and other features.Brookfield will lead the preparation of the plan, while both the developer and the city are hiring consultants to help with the work. The process is expected to begin this winter.The redevelopment plan is much larger than the 2,422 acres covered by the financial agreement. According to SFGATE, the wider plans include 12,272 housing units, a 75-acre first responder training facility, a 4-acre veterans community centre and a $5 million sports park.The plans also include 5,038 acres for Thurgood Marshall Regional Park, 16 acres for permanently supportive housing and 10 acres for food bank expansion.The project is expected to take decades to complete. City officials have said the build-out could span 30 years, while the Specific Plan is expected to be presented to the Concord City Council in summer 2029.Community input plannedThe project will also move into a new phase of community engagement. Additional discussions with residents are expected to begin in early 2027 as Concord and Brookfield work on the Specific Plan and other documents needed for the development.Brookfield became the project's master developer in 2023 after Lennar, the original developer, withdrew from the project in 2020 following a dispute with labour organisers.The Navy's latest approval follows the Concord City Council's approval of the financial agreement in late May. With the two approvals in place, the city and Brookfield can now focus on turning the broader redevelopment vision into a detailed plan.Guy Bjerke, Concord's director of economic development and base reuse, described the Navy's approval as an important milestone. Bjerke is retiring on September 30, this year, after 11 years in his current role.“I am proud the Base Reuse Project has reached this important milestone. The US Navy has proven to be a tremendous partner in moving the community’s vision forward. This approval moves the Project into an important next phase, and our dedicated staff will continue working diligently to advance the Specific Plan,” Bjerke said as quoted by Contra Costa Herald.The next major steps will involve detailed planning, consultant work and further discussions with the community. The Specific Plan will eventually provide the framework for how the former naval weapons station is developed.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: AC bus booked but passenger given non-AC ride, dropped 10 km before destination; consumer court orders Rs 31,500
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Visakhapatnam district consumer commission has directed a bus operator to pay Rs 31,500 to a passenger who was charged for an AC bus but
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Visakhapatnam district consumer commission has directed a bus operator to pay Rs 31,500 to a passenger who was charged for an AC bus but made to travel in a non-AC bus and dropped around 9-10 km before his destination at midnight. The commission awarded Rs 30,000 as compensation for mental harassment and Rs 1,000 as litigation costs. The order was passed on September 15.Why did the passenger approach the consumer commission?The complainant booked a bus journey from Hyderabad to Rajahmundry by paying Rs 1,200 through PhonePe. He alleged that he was assured that the journey would be in an AC bus but was instead made to travel in a non-AC bus, as per the commission order.The passenger further alleged that despite paying the fare, he was not given a physical ticket or booking slip and also was dropped around 9-10 km away from his destination.The complainant then claimed that he had to make arrangements for further transportation at midnight, causing inconvenience and hardship. He approached the bus operator seeking a refund of Rs 500, but said the request was refused.He later approached the national consumer helpline, but the complaint was disposed of without resolution due to procedural reasons. The bus operator did not respond to the consumer complaint and remained absent despite being served notice.What did the commission find?The bench comprising President Gudla Tanuja and members Varri Krishna Murthy and Rahimunnisa Begum examined the payment record and other documents submitted by the passenger. It found that Rs 1,200 had been paid for the journey and that the passenger had booked travel in an AC bus.The commission noted that the bus operator received the fare for an AC service but made the passenger travel in a non-AC bus. It also found that he was dropped at Kovvuru instead of Rajahmundry, despite the fare being paid for travel to Rajahmundry."The complainant's agony is that he booked a bus journey ticket with the opposite party for the journey from Hyderabad to Rajahmundry by paying an amount of Rs.1,200/- for journey by AC bus whereas the complainant was made to travel by a non-ac bus. Despite payment of the fare of Rs.1,200/- no physical ticket/booking slip was handed over to him by the opposite party," the commission observed.The commission said the passenger had been put to inconvenience, hardship, additional expenditure and mental agony because he had to arrange onward transportation from Kovvuru late at night."The opposite party falls also under the purview of deficiency of service for forcibly dropping the complainant at Kovvuru (which is around 9 to 10 kms from Rajahmundry) instead of Rajahmundry for which an consideration was received. In view of the above pleadings point No 1 is answered in favour of the complainant and against the opposite party," the commission added.The commission held that the bus operator could not avoid liability for providing a non-AC bus when it had received the fare for an AC service. It also held that dropping the passenger at Kovvuru instead of Rajahmundry amounted to deficiency in service.What did the consumer commission order?The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission-I, Visakhapatnam, directed the bus operator to:Pay Rs 500 towards the difference between the AC and non-AC fares.Pay Rs 30,000 as compensation for mental harassment.Pay Rs 1,000 towards litigation costs.Make the payment within 30 days from receiving the order.The commission further directed that if the amount was not paid within 30 days, the total amount of Rs 31,500 would carry annual interest at 9 percent from March 6, 2026, the date of the journey, until realisation.

articles.title: In 1982, Paul Newman started selling homemade salad dressing and gave away the profits; 40 years later, his company has donated over $600 million
articles.summary: In 1980, Paul Newman and his friend A.E. Hotchner were not setting out to build a food company.
articles.body: In 1980, Paul Newman and his friend A.E. Hotchner were not setting out to build a food company. They were making salad dressing at home and handing bottles to friends as Christmas presents. The dressing proved popular enough that people began asking where they could get more. Two years later, the experiment became Newman’s Own, with Newman deciding that the profits should be given away rather than kept by the business. What began with a familiar kitchen product gradually developed into a wider philanthropic enterprise. According to Newman’s Own Foundation, more than four decades later, the company says more than $600 million has been donated to charitable causes, while its founder’s name remains closely tied to the idea behind the business.Newman’s Own turned an unexpected profit into a charitable missionNewman and Hotchner made salad dressing for friends around 1980, initially treating it as a holiday gift rather than the beginning of a commercial venture. Friends wanted to buy the dressing, and the pair eventually decided to put it on the market. Newman’s Own officially launched in 1982, and the first year produced more than $300,000 in profit.Newman then made a decision that would define the company. Rather than treating the unexpected earnings as personal income, he and Hotchner chose to give the money to charitable causes. The phrase associated with that decision was simple: “Let’s give it all away to those who need it!”The arrangement became the foundation of the business model. Consumers bought the products, the company generated profits, and those profits were directed towards causes rather than building personal wealth for Newman.Paul Newman’s career reached beyond Hollywood into racing and social causesBy the time Newman’s Own appeared, Newman was already one of Hollywood’s best-known actors. His career had begun on Broadway in 1958 with Picnic, where he also met Joanne Woodward and became his wife.Reportedly, film success followed. Newman appeared in more than 50 films, including The Hustler, Hud, Cool Hand Luke, Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid, The Sting, Slap Shot and Road to Perdition. His performance in The Color of Money earned him the Academy Award for best actor in 1987. Away from acting, he developed another serious interest in motor racing. His public life also extended into political and social causes. Newman attended the March on Washington in 1963 and spoke publicly on civil rights, women's rights and gay rights. He also campaigned against the nuclear arms race and was appointed by President Jimmy Carter to a United Nations General Assembly session concerning nuclear disarmament.The charitable work that later became inseparable from his name therefore developed alongside an already established public career.The camp gave the philanthropy a physical homeNewman’s interest in helping children became particularly visible in 1988, when the Hole in the Wall Gang Camp opened in Connecticut. The camp was created for children with serious illnesses. Its first year brought 288 children through its programme, with the setting designed to give them an ordinary camp experience away from hospitals and medical routines.The project eventually became part of SeriousFun Children’s Network, the organisation connected to Newman’s broader philanthropic legacy. The camp also illustrated a feature of his giving that went beyond writing cheques. His charitable interests increasingly involved creating organisations and programmes that could operate over time.How his daughter helped expand the food businessThe Newman family became involved in the food company in other ways too. In 1993, Newman’s daughter Nell Newman founded Newman’s Own Organics with her father and business partner Peter Meehan. The venture broadened the range of food associated with the Newman’s Own name. Paul Newman’s daughter Melissa Newman was also involved creatively, designing the American Gothic-inspired label featuring Paul alongside Nell.By then, the original salad dressing experiment had become something much larger. The business included a growing range of products, while its profits continued to be linked to charitable giving.A foundation was created before Newman’s deathNewman established Newman’s Own Foundation in 2005, creating a structure intended to preserve the charitable purpose of the business beyond his lifetime. He died on 26 September 2008, aged 83. The foundation was designed to continue distributing money generated through Newman’s Own. The basic principle established in the early 1980s remained intact: the commercial side of the business existed to generate money that could be directed towards good causes.A legal change helped protect the modelThe unusual relationship between a commercial food company and a private foundation later required a different legal framework. In 2018, the Philanthropic Enterprise Act was passed, allowing a for-profit company to be entirely owned by a private foundation and operate with the purpose of giving its profits to charitable causes.For Newman’s Own, the change provided a legal structure through which the company could continue the model Newman had established decades earlier. The business was no longer simply a celebrity-branded food company. Its ownership and purpose had been structured around philanthropy.More than $600 million had been donated by 2022Newman’s Own marked its 40th anniversary in 2022 and reported that more than $600 million had been donated to charitable causes. The foundation's work was also being concentrated around areas connected to children facing adversity. Its priorities included nutrition education and school food, Indigenous food justice, and SeriousFun Children’s Network.That represented a more defined focus than the broad charitable giving associated with the company's early years. The money raised through products could support programmes dealing with food, children and community needs in different ways.The scale of the giving is striking partly because of how ordinary the original product was. Salad dressing was the starting point. The business model that grew around it became the mechanism for distributing hundreds of millions of dollars.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Le Pen hails ‘historic victory’ as far-right secures senate group ahead of 2027 presidential polls
articles.summary: Marine Le Pen’s far-right National Rally (RN) has secured enough seats to form a parliamentary group in France’s Senate for the first time, marking a
articles.body: Marine Le Pen’s far-right National Rally (RN) has secured enough seats to form a parliamentary group in France’s Senate for the first time, marking a breakthrough for the party less than a year before the 2027 presidential election.The RN and its smaller ally, the Union of the Right for the Republic (UDR), will have at least 15 seats in the 348-member upper house, exceeding the minimum 10 required to form a group. The results of the weekend election were published on Monday.The RN won nine seats, while the UDR, led by Eric Ciotti, secured three. The party’s presence in the Senate will allow it to participate in influential committees that examine and shape legislation."This is a historic victory, and a major milestone with the formation for the first time of a group in the Senate," Le Pen said on X.RN president Jordan Bardella, who is eyeing the post of prime minister if Le Pen becomes president, said the results confirmed "the momentum of our movement as we approach the mother of all battles -- the presidential election"."If our compatriots so desire, we will very soon govern France," he said.Le Pen leads presidential pollThe Senate results came as a new Toluna-Harris survey for French television channels RTL and M6 showed Le Pen leading the first round of the 2027 presidential election, scheduled for April 18, with 35% to 36% of the vote.The poll projected that she would reach the run-off against hard-left France Unbowed (LFI) leader Jean-Luc Melenchon, who was seen securing 17% to 18%. Centrist hopeful Edouard Philippe was projected to win 13% to 16%.In the second round, Le Pen was projected to defeat both Melenchon and Philippe. She was seen winning 69% of the vote against Melenchon and 57% against Philippe.The survey was conducted from September 22 to 24. A previous poll published on September 14 had put Le Pen at 33% in the first round.RN expands presence in SenateThe Senate is elected indirectly by local elected officials, with half of its members chosen every three years for six-year terms. The chamber has traditionally been dominated by the right and shares legislative responsibilities with the lower National Assembly.The RN first entered the Senate in 2014, when it was known as the National Front, winning two seats. It secured three seats in 2023. The latest results take the far-right party and its ally to at least 15 seats.The Republicans (LR), the main right-wing party, are expected to retain their dominance in the Senate despite losing seats. Senate speaker Gerard Larcher, 77, is also expected to remain in office.The left-wing LFI won its first-ever Senate seat.The RN emerged as the largest single party in the National Assembly after President Emmanuel Macron called snap elections in 2024, but fell short of securing a majority.French daily Le Monde described the Senate results as a "warning", saying they showed "the extent to which the RN has established itself within our institutions in barely ten years"."The far-right breakthrough was expected, and the result does not alter the Senate majority... Yet a new threshold has been crossed," it added.Hollande keeps 2027 presidential bid openMeanwhile, former French president Francois Hollande has said he may consider contesting the 2027 presidential election, but only if he sees a realistic chance of winning."Running for the presidency is not a decision to be taken lightly, all the more so for a former head of state like myself," Hollande told Italian daily La Repubblica on Monday.The 72-year-old, who served as president from 2012 to 2017, said he would consider entering the race only under exceptional circumstances and if he had a realistic possibility of reaching the run-off and ultimately winning."The France of 2027 bears little resemblance to the one I governed. We are facing a more threatening, more dangerous and harsher world, and a European continent that has become a target for powers such as the United States, China and Russia. Europe is confronting an existential crisis," Hollande said.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 'If the system is being gamed...': New York's Rochester General Hospital accused of hiring 80 H-1Bs of J-1s, only 2 Americans
articles.summary: A viral post accused New York's Rochester General Hospital of hiring a maximum of foreign doctors instead of Americans amid the ongoing H-1B controversy.
articles.body: A viral post accused New York's Rochester General Hospital of hiring a maximum of foreign doctors instead of Americans amid the ongoing H-1B controversy. The post to which the hospital has not yet commented, claimed that the hospital has 82 resident doctors and that, among them, only two are Americans -- 80 are foreign workers on either H-1B or J-1 visas. "98% of the residency slots went to visa workers- mostly from countries with documented USMLE cheating. Americans got 2 jobs," the post claimed.While such anti-H-1B allegations are abundant on social media, Department of Labor inspector general Anthony D'Esposito commented on this post and asked the hospital if the allegation was right."@ROCRegional: Show us the numbers. How many residency slots went to H‑1B and J‑1 visa holders? How many American applicants got a fair shot? @POTUS’ EO puts visa abuse under the microscope. If the system is being gamed, we’ll work with @VP’s @WHFraudTF to expose it," D'Esposito said.H-1B visa program is meant for hiring skilled foreign workers. J-1 visa is a temporary, non-immigrant visa for approved work or study exchange programs.'What is the problem if foreign workers are doctors'Social media users reacted to D'Esposito's warning and wondered what the problem was if foreign workers are as high skilled as doctors."I hope you all do realize that you have more residency spot than American graduates, so foreigners often come in and take a spot that would be empty otherwise? This is internal medicine. They’re not taking Americans spots, they’re taking spots that are left over and without them you’ll just have a doctor left. There is ZERO benefit for a hospital to pick a foreign medical graduate over an American one. If anything it adds cost as they have to pay for the whole visa process," one doctor commented.The social media account that made the allegation against the hospital claimed that American doctors "are forced" to leave after foreign workers flooded the department. articles.title: South Africa's degraded Eastern Cape is getting 180 million spekboom plants; the restoration project is expected to create 11,000 jobs
articles.summary: South Africa’s Eastern Cape is set to undergo a major land restoration effort centred on spekboom, a hardy succulent that grows naturally in the region.
articles.body: South Africa’s Eastern Cape is set to undergo a major land restoration effort centred on spekboom, a hardy succulent that grows naturally in the region. According to Amazon, this investment will help restore more than 50,000 hectares of degraded land and plant 180 million spekboom cuttings by the end of 2028. The programme is expected to create around 11,000 jobs by 2030 and generate more than $500 million in economic value.The restoration focuses on the declining Albany thicket, where years of land use have affected the landscape and its ability to support nature and communities. As part of the project, Amazon will purchase 1.95 million tonnes of nature-based carbon removal credits generated over more than a decade. The first phase is already underway across 10,000 hectares.How will 180 million spekboom cuttings help restore the Albany thicketMore than 50,000 hectares will be added to the project as a result of Amazon's support. The project centres on spekboom, a hardy succulent that grows in the region’s harsh climate. By the end of 2028, 180 million spekboom cuttings will be planted across the landscape. The effort focuses on the Albany thicket, a distinctive ecosystem that has been in decline for decades. The project is already underway, with its first phase beginning in April 2024. That phase covers 10,000 hectares and includes 30 million plants. The programme is designed and operated by ecosystem restorers Imperative.Why is spekboom important for restoring the Eastern CapeSpekboom is central to the restoration because it evolved specifically for the Eastern Cape’s harsh climate. It is locally known as elephant bush because elephants browse its leaves; the succulent grows in harsh conditions where many other plants cannot. It grows from simple cuttings placed directly into the soil, making restoration practical at enormous scale. As the plants mature, they cool the landscape around them and improve depleted soils.They also create conditions for ecosystems to recover naturally. The area is home to 165 recorded plant and animal species, including several considered vulnerable by conservationists. Scientists have found that spekboom can remove carbon from the atmosphere at rates comparable to young tropical forests. The United Nations has also named spekboom restoration one of its World Restoration Flagship initiatives.How will the restoration project create jobs and support local communitiesThe programme is expected to create around 11,000 jobs by 2030 in one of South Africa’s most economically disadvantaged regions. According to Amazon, the programme will also train local businesses. The project is expected to bring over $500 million into surrounding communities through wages, procurement, landowner payments and community investment.Amazon has committed to purchase 1.95 million tons of carbon removal credits generated by the project over more than a decade. The commitment enabled the World Bank to launch a Spekboom Outcome Bond, which gives investors confidence that there would be a buyer for the project’s future credits.The credits are available for qualified companies to purchase through Amazon’s carbon credit service. They will carry both the ABACUS label and Climate, Community & Biodiversity (CCB) certification.How does the restoration project support carbon removalThe project is part of Amazon’s work towards its Climate Pledge goal of reaching net-zero carbon across its operations by 2040. Its purchase of 1.95 million tonnes of carbon removal credits is one of the largest private-sector commitments to nature restoration in South Africa’s history. The project has also received an ‘AA.pre’ Standalone Rating from BeZeroCarbon, an independent agency that assesses the quality of carbon credits.The rating ranges from AAA, the highest, to D, the lowest, and indicates a high level of confidence that the project’s credits represent real, verified carbon dioxide removal. Amazon says the project is among the highest-rated afforestation, reforestation and revegetation projects in the world. Together, the programme combines land restoration and carbon removal with local employment and investment in surrounding communities.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.summary: Van-Houston McMillion is fourteen years old, an age when most children are settling into their first year of high school, yet he has just begun his
articles.body: Van-Houston McMillion is fourteen years old, an age when most children are settling into their first year of high school, yet he has just begun his sophomore year at Calhoun Community College in Huntsville, Alabama. He enrolled at twelve, becoming the youngest student in the college's history, according to Calhoun Community College, and he is now pursuing his passion for chemistry. As reported by WAFF 48, McMillion expects to complete his degree around this time next year, which could see him finish before turning sixteen. Here is how his journey began, how his first year unfolded, and what comes next.How Van-Houston McMillion's early love of learning led to college at age 12Long before he set foot on a college campus, McMillion was showing signs of unusual ability. According to Calhoun Community College, his mother, Emma-Sara McMillion, noticed his exceptional ability to learn around the age of two, when he began identifying letters and sounding out words. By the time most children were learning their alphabet, he was reading street signs aloud, watching science documentaries and asking questions well beyond his years. After years of individualised homeschooling focused on mastery rather than memorisation, he took a standardised college admissions test as a benchmark, and his high scores confirmed he was ready for a more structured and challenging setting.Enrolling at Calhoun Community College and admissions conversationsThe next step followed a series of thorough conversations between McMillion's family and Calhoun's admissions team and faculty. Those discussions considered not only academic readiness but also his emotional maturity, learning style and long-term aspirations. In the fall of 2025, he began working toward an Associate of Science in General Education with a focus on chemistry, taking a mix of in-person and online courses including American National Government, English Composition I, Freshman Seminar, Intermediate College Algebra, Precalculus Algebra and Music Appreciation. Doctor Jimmy Hodges, the college's president, said McMillion is a shining example of what happens when curiosity, hard work and community come together.A steep learning curve: McMillion's first year of collegeMcMillion's first year was not without its challenges. He told WAFF 48 that navigating college coursework came with a steep learning curve that required strict time management. “Some days were stressful,” and he learned that procrastination “is not at all an option." His discipline paid off: he completed his historic freshman year with a 3.5 grade point average, earning a spot on the college's Dean's List. Now beginning his sophomore year at fourteen, McMillion expects to be done with his degree around this time next year, adding that he can barely believe it.Career goals; what McMillion says comes next for himThose who know McMillion best say his character leaves the greatest impression. His mother told Calhoun Community College that he is grounded and kind, never acts like he is better than anyone else, and simply wants to learn and make a difference rather than be the youngest. Wes Rakestraw, the college's Vice President of Academics, said that although McMillion is young in age, he brings a level of discipline and drive that inspires everyone. McMillion hopes to explore innovative ways to solve real-world problems, start impactful businesses and study systems deeply in order to improve them. articles.summary: Flooding continued in several low-lying areas of Thailand’s capital Bangkok on Sunday despite a decline in rainfall, leaving more than 3,000 people in
articles.body: Flooding continued in several low-lying areas of Thailand’s capital Bangkok on Sunday despite a decline in rainfall, leaving more than 3,000 people in temporary shelters and disrupting transport and commercial activity.At least eight people have died nationwide in the past 10 days, while floods have affected more than 545,000 people across 25 provinces, particularly in central and eastern Thailand, according to the Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation.More than 200 temporary shelters have been set up across Bangkok, with over 3,000 people still staying there as of Sunday. Officials said 31 routes remained affected by flooding.Days of continuous rain, with cumulative rainfall reaching 30 centimetres in some areas, have caused extensive flooding in the capital. Several low-lying neighbourhoods, particularly in suburban areas, remained inundated, forcing residents to evacuate.Bangkok Governor Chadchart Sittipunt said rainfall had eased and municipal authorities were working to drain water from affected areas. However, he warned that water levels in the city’s main canals remained high, with some continuing to rise as water flowed in from surrounding areas.Thailand’s Meteorological Department forecast improving conditions from Monday, although moderate to heavy rain was still expected in several parts of the country on Sunday.Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul said excessive rainfall had caused flooding in areas where water levels exceeded drainage capacity. He directed relevant authorities to respond quickly, ease the situation and provide assistance to those affected.Long-distance bus and rail services were suspended on several routes. articles.title: 'Have you ever voted in US election?' 61-year-old Canadian citizen, US Green Card holder, detained at border, interrogated for 6 hours, made to sign removal order
articles.summary: A 61-year-old Canadian citizen who has been living in the US for 14 years as a Green Card holder was detained by border officials and interrogated for
articles.body: A 61-year-old Canadian citizen who has been living in the US for 14 years as a Green Card holder was detained by border officials and interrogated for hours about whether she ever voted for any US election. Paige Adamson told CBC News that she was on her way home from a birthday dinner in Tsawwassen, British Columbia, Canada, while her residence is in Point Roberts, Washington State, in the US.Two places at the center of the issuePoint Roberts is a US territory, but it is physically cut off from the rest of Washington State by Canadian territory. So someone who lives in the United States in Point Roberts like Adamson can routinely have to cross into Canada and then re-enter the United States to go elsewhere in the region.Point Roberts is called a pene-exclave of the US state of Washington on the southernmost tip of the Tsawwassen peninsula, south of Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada.'Have you ever voted in a federal US election'Adamson told the CBC News that the first question she was asked was whether she ever voted in a federal US election. She regularly crossed the border but this was the first time she was stopped and asked this question. "They immediately said, 'Park over here and come into the office.'"Adamson said she told them that she never voted in the US but the Department of Homeland Security accused her of falsely claiming that she was a US citizen and that she voted. She was interrogated for six hours until after 2am and was made to sign documents before being admitted to the US. One of the documents CBC News reviewed said Adamson "must surrender for removal from the United States, if so ordered."The DHS said Adamson registered to vote in Whatcom County, Washington State. She also voted in Washington State's 2018 general election, it has been alleged. Adamson said she never voted in a federal election and did not remember ever voting in a state election but she received a ballot once and may have been registered."I was basically treated like a criminal," she said, recounting the experience of the interrogation. articles.title: A Pennsylvania dairy farmer spent 70 years watching bears and turkeys on his 170-acre farm; in 2026, after turning down two lucrative offers, he permanently protected the land from development
articles.summary: For 70 years, Jeff Biddle has lived and worked on Bear Meadows Farm near Tussey Mountain in Pennsylvania.
articles.body: For 70 years, Jeff Biddle has lived and worked on Bear Meadows Farm near Tussey Mountain in Pennsylvania. He has raised cattle, grown crops and watched bears, turkeys, deer and waterfowl from the woods around his home. In July this year, Biddle permanently protected the 170-acre farm from development after turning down two lucrative offers from buyers, according to the Centre County Farmland Trust (CCFT).Biddle finalised a conservation easement with CCFT in July. The legally binding agreement prevents the land from being developed and is attached to the property deed, meaning the protection will remain even if the farm changes ownership in the future.Biddle had been thinking about preserving the farm for about 30 years. He rejected two offers from interested buyers, including one who told him he could make a lot of money from the property and pointed to its beauty.“And I said ‘Yes, I do,’ have a beautiful property,” Biddle said. “And that’s because there’s no houses on it, which is true. I mean, once you build houses and look at rooftops, it’s not beautiful anymore. It’s a nice development,” he added.For Biddle, the farm represents decades of work and memories. He remembers picking rocks from its fields as a child and did not want to see that work replaced by development.“Honestly, I have been picking rocks off this farm ever since I was a little kid. We grow a lot of rocks here. I don’t know how many tons and tons and tons of rocks I have picked off this farm. And to see a bulldozer come in and take all those years of hard work and not care- no,” he said.Agriculture and wildlife protectedThe conservation easement will keep Bear Meadows Farm protected from development while allowing it to remain available for agriculture. The farm’s fields, forests and open land provide benefits for water quality and wildlife habitat.The land also contains trees and soil that store carbon. Its open fields will remain visible from Route 322 for residents and visitors to Centre County.The farm is near the edge of the Centre Region’s 'growth boundary'. Dan Guss, president of CCFT, said its fields and forests are also important to the headwaters of Spring Creek.“Bear Meadows Farm is a beautiful, well-run farm located on the edge of the ‘growth boundary’ for the Centre Region,” Guss said. “The fields and forests on the farm are an important groundwater resource for the Spring Creek headwaters,” he added.The conservation agreement was made possible through a partnership between CCFT and ClearWater Conservancy. ClearWater helped with technical and legal work, easement documents, mapping and fieldwork.“Preserving the Bear Meadows Farm not only protects a loved family dairy farm but also advances the Upper Spring Creek Watershed Coldwater Conservation Plan and maintains scenic open space in our growing region,” said Ryan Hamilton, ClearWater Conservancy’s Director of Land Conservation.Farm connects to Spring Creek watershedThe property is also connected to the wider Spring Creek watershed. ClearWater Conservancy has worked for more than 30 years to protect the watershed and land around its headwaters.The watershed includes surface streams, groundwater and subsurface aquifers. It provides drinking water, habitat for wild trout and opportunities for outdoor recreation and tourism.Bear Meadows Farm contains a historic spring house from which the headwaters of an unnamed tributary to Spring Creek flow. The property also has two other unnamed tributaries and two ponds fed by seepage springs.A Baseline Documentation Report prepared by ClearWater as part of the conservation easement said water from the farm flows towards Spring Creek.“All of the seeps and streams on the Bear Meadows Farm Property flow in a northerly direction to Spring Creek, which flows to Bald Eagle Creek, to the West Branch of the Susquehanna River, and finally, the Susquehanna River, a major contributor to the Chesapeake Bay,” the report said.The farm includes 50 acres of pasture and hay and 11 acres of cultivated crops. It also has 55 acres of deciduous forest, 13 acres of evergreen forest, 26 acres of mixed forest and four acres of grassland.From family farm to dairy operationBiddle’s connection to the property began with his father, Harold Biddle, who bought six acres in the woods for a hunting camp before purchasing the 175-acre property in 1959. He restored the barn, repaired outbuildings and raised beef cattle.Jeff grew up on the farm before leaving to become a cabinet-maker and run his own woodworking business. He continued helping his father with the beef operation while raising his family with his wife, Claudia.Dairy farming, however, had always been an ambition. “For some reason, ever since I was a kid I wanted to have a dairy farm,” Biddle said. “I don’t know why.”When Biddle was 49, he and Claudia were preparing to buy a farm in Mifflin County. Instead, he and his father agreed to change the operation at Bear Meadows Farm. Jeff and Claudia took over the farm in 2002.Three years later, they converted it to a grass-based dairy. In 2009, they received a permit from the Pennsylvania Department of Agriculture to sell raw milk. Biddle calls his move into dairy farming his “mid-life crisis”.Today, the farm raises grass-fed dairy cows and sells raw milk, ground beef and eggs. It also sells about 10 types of cheese made from the farm’s milk by an off-site cheesemaker.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 'Naive gamer' to IS sympathiser: How US teen Daniel Fischer was radicalised
articles.summary: An American boy who went from being a “naive gamer” to embracing an “extreme vision” of Islam became an IS “sympathiser” and eventually a convict working
articles.body: An American boy who went from being a “naive gamer” to embracing an “extreme vision” of Islam became an IS “sympathiser” and eventually a convict working to leave extremist ideology.Daniel Fischer from South Carolina was just 16 when his parents noticed a sudden change in his behaviour.The American teenager became deeply interested in extremist content online, started arguing with his family about religion and eventually told investigators that he wanted to join IS, according to a CNN report.His parents, Ana and Andy Fischer, became concerned after their younger son told them Daniel was watching beheading videos. They took away his phone and PlayStation and tried other ways to intervene, but nothing seemed to work.When FBI and South Carolina law enforcement officers later searched his home, they found two phones, two weapons, a laptop and a journal detailing plans to join IS and kill people, the report said.Daniel was arrested on state charges linked to terrorism and bomb threats. He later pleaded guilty to a conspiracy charge and was sentenced in June to three years in prison and five years of probation.His case highlights a wider concern over teenagers being radicalised online in the US. Since 2024, most of the 19 IS-inspired plots and attacks in the country involved at least one teenager, according to the Institute for Strategic Dialogue, a nonprofit research group cited by CNN.FBI deputy director Christopher Raia said that the age of people turning to extremism is falling, making such cases more difficult for investigators and prosecutors.“The ages of those turning to extremism are getting younger every year, challenging our investigative methods, and complicating the ability for prosecutors to bring federal charges,” Raia said.Experts told CNN that teenagers dealing with loneliness, identity problems or emotional distress can be vulnerable to extremist messaging online. Such groups can offer them a sense of purpose and belonging.Daniel later told a court that he had been going through an identity crisis and had “found myself speaking to the wrong people”.He has also been working with Parents for Peace, a group that helps people leave extremist movements. Its counsellor Mubin Shaikh said IS had given Daniel “that purpose, that meaning, that belonging and that identity”.The FBI said the trend is not limited to one form of extremism. Raia said the rise in juvenile radicalisation involves both domestic and international extremist ideologies.Several other recent cases have involved young Americans accused of IS-inspired plots, underlining concerns about how quickly online radicalisation can turn into plans for violence.You use AI every day. articles.title: ‘I hid the truth’: Pro-Palestinian activist Hanna Gann spent years claiming Palestinian, Black roots in US; finally admits she is White Jewish
articles.summary: Hanna Gann, a high school teacher and pro-Palestinian activist, reveals her true White Jewish heritage after being confronted about her misrepresented racial and ethnic background, leading to backlash from activist groups and her community.
articles.body: A Philadelphia high school teacher and pro-Palestinian activist has acknowledged that she spent years misrepresenting her racial and ethnic background, at times presenting herself as Palestinian, Tunisian, and Black.Hanna Gann, who teaches at The Workshop School, admitted the deception after activists confronted her about her background during a meeting earlier this month, according to the Philadelphia Inquirer.The Racial Justice Organising Committee (RJOC) and Philly Educators for Palestine (PEFP) said in a September 19 statement that Gann was questioned for more than an hour before acknowledging that she had lied. The groups said they had ended their association with her and called on her to publicly acknowledge that she is “a white woman of Jewish heritage and an Israeli settler family.Gann later addressed the allegations herself in a series of Instagram posts and a 10-minute video published on September 21.“I hid the truth or outright lied about my background to everyone in my life,” Gann said. She described herself as “a white woman of significant privilege and wealth” and said she had allowed “half-truths and obfuscations” to develop into lies.Gann had become known in Philadelphia for her activism in support of Palestinians and for mentoring disadvantaged Black students. The Philadelphia Inquirer reported that she took part in a 2024 West Philadelphia teach-in focused on “scholasticide”, a term used to describe the destruction of educational infrastructure in Gaza. Her biography for the event described her as Palestinian American.She also supported Philadelphia teacher Keziah Ridgeway, who faced disciplinary action over private pro-Palestinian social media posts and later sued the school district, alleging anti-Islamic bias.Questions about her claimed background intensified after documents compiled by the Philly Palestine Coalition and reviewed by the Inquirer challenged some of the family history she had previously described.According to the newspaper, Gann had repeatedly referred to Palestinian relatives, including a grandfather she said was born in Palestine. Historical draft records and naturalisation documents examined by the coalition indicated that the grandfather was born in Baltimore.Gann had told people she was struggling financially because she was sending money to relatives in Palestine, and that some people subsequently gave her money.A former University of Pennsylvania classmate told the outlet that Gann had previously described herself in college as a white Jewish woman with family in the occupied West Bank. The classmate also alleged that Gann changed her appearance and manner of speaking after returning to Philadelphia from the Peace Corps in Rwanda.Gann did not dispute the broader allegations in her Instagram statement. She said she had concealed her background from people around her but maintained that her involvement in the causes she supported was genuine.“One of the most sickening aspects of facing what I’ve done is seeing the way that the blowback is falling on people, groups, communities and causes I genuinely care about,” she said.Gann also asked people not to treat her actions as evidence that other pro-Palestinian activists were acting dishonestly.“The fact that I lied about who I was does not mean anyone else who speaks up for Palestine is lying and does not erase the urgency of listening to voices on the ground,” she said.The two Philadelphia activist groups said Gann's actions had damaged trust among the communities and organisations with which she worked.“We are stunned, saddened and angered by the betrayal. We will no longer work with Hanna, and she will no longer be welcome at our organising spaces,” RJOC and PEFP said in their joint statement.The groups said they believed her conduct had harmed Palestinians whose identity and struggle had been appropriated, as well as members of the Black community, young people, organisers and organisations whose trust and resources had been used.The Philadelphia School District said it was aware of social media posts concerning a district employee and her involvement with an outside advocacy organisation.“The school district of Philadelphia is aware of social media posts concerning a district employee and her involvement with an outside advocacy organization,” a district spokesperson told the Guardian. “The posts reference the employee’s involvement in an external group. The district is making support available to The Workshop School staff and students, as needed.”You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A Texas landowner bought a ranch in the 1990s and later added thousands of acres; today, more than 7,000 acres are managed for mule deer, pronghorn and other wildlife
articles.summary: Tim Delaney had no family history of ranching when he bought Rolling Thunder Ranch in Wyoming in 2010.
articles.body: Tim Delaney had no family history of ranching when he bought Rolling Thunder Ranch in Wyoming in 2010. He and his wife had spent years visiting Colorado, but they wanted a property of their own where they could combine recreation with agriculture. Today, Delaney manages thousands of acres for wildlife, recreation and livestock.Delaney, who lives in upstate New York, is also a principal in a heavy highway construction firm that builds large commercial wind farms and infrastructure such as roads and bridges, according to US Deprtament of Agriculture. His family had raised draft horses and some cattle on a small scale, but Rolling Thunder Ranch was his first major ranching experience.The Wyoming property sits at about 8,500 feet and covers a landscape that Delaney describes as a large bowl surrounded by mountain ranges. The ranch provides habitat for a wide range of wildlife, including moose, grizzly bears, elk, deer, pronghorn, black bears, sage grouse, mountain lions and wolves.Since buying the property, Delaney has also worked on conservation projects. With help from The Conservation Fund and the US Department of Agriculture’s Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS), he has used conservation easements to protect the land. He has also regenerated aspen stands and replaced 20 miles of conventional fencing with wildlife-friendly fencing.Bying the Delaney Wyoming ranchDelaney said he and his family had been spending time in Colorado since the late 1990s. Over the years, the property they visited was gradually being sold in pieces, reducing their opportunities for hiking, hunting and fishing.That led them to look for a property that could provide both recreational and agricultural uses. In late 2009, they found Rolling Thunder Ranch and decided to buy it. They completed the purchase in spring 2010.The family spends about 10 to 12 weeks at the ranch each year. From November to mid-May, however, the property is usually covered by snow. A neighbouring rancher leases summer grazing rights on the land, and 600 head of yearlings grazed there in the year described in the Farmers.gov report.For Delaney, the ranch stood out because of its landscape and wildlife habitat. He said the property offers views of three mountain ranges and allows visitors to see almost the entire perimeter from its higher areas.Deciding to conserve the areaDelaney said owning the ranch gave him an opportunity to become involved in conservation, even though his professional background is in construction.“As I said, I am in the construction business, so when you own a bulldozer for a living, you are not considered necessarily to be conservation minded,” he said.He said he approached improvements on the ranch with the same planning mindset he uses in construction. That approach also led him to undertake wider conservation planning for the property.According to Delaney, the conservation work made economic sense as well as supporting the land. He said it could benefit both the future value of the ranch and its agricultural operation.“Our experience has been that conservation can certainly go hand-in-hand with ranching- they are mutually beneficial,” Delaney said.His work with The Conservation Fund began after Luke Lynch, then the organisation’s Wyoming state director, contacted him. Lynch explained how conservation easements could help landowners protect working properties.Lynch also connected Delaney with funding from the NRCS. The funding was used for conservation easements that helped protect working land on the ranch.More than 7,900 acres covered Delaney and his partners eventually completed three bargain sales of conservation easements covering several connected pieces of land.The first covered the original 3,600 acres of Rolling Thunder Ranch. A few years later, Delaney purchased another 4,000 acres at Rim Ranch, which was also included in the conservation work. A further 340-acre former subdivision lot, called Rolling Thunder II, was also protected. Together, the three properties cover 7,940 acres.The 340-acre Rolling Thunder II property has particular importance for migrating mule deer and pronghorn. Delaney said the land lies entirely within a stop-over area on the mule deer migration route.Hundreds of mule deer have been seen moving through the property during their spring and autumn migrations. The ranch properties are also located within habitat areas designated by the Wyoming Game and Fish Department for sage grouse.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Archaeologists uncover rare Roman-era workshop in Germany with pottery kiln and furnaces used to recycle Roman metal
articles.summary: Archaeologists have uncovered a rare Roman-era workshop area in western Dortmund, Germany, during an excavation of a settlement dating from the 1st to 5th
articles.body: Archaeologists have uncovered a rare Roman-era workshop area in western Dortmund, Germany, during an excavation of a settlement dating from the 1st to 5th centuries AD. The site contains several areas with pits, furnaces, and hearths. It also has the first pottery kiln found at the site and exceptionally well-preserved workshops used for metalworking. The excavation team from the Landschaftsverband Westfalen-Lippe (LWL) and the Dortmund City Archaeology Department began examining the settlement in mid-August. Reportedly, the workshop area is a first of its kind in the western part of the Germanic settlement area.Archaeologists uncover a rare workshop area in western DortmundThe excavation team has uncovered several areas used for craft work at the settlement. The remains include pits, furnaces and hearths that provide evidence of different activities carried out at the site.The excavation team also identified the first pottery kiln discovered at the site. The team also identified workshops used for metalworking. These areas are described as exceptionally well preserved. Dr Eva Cichy, excavation director at the Olpe branch of LWL Archaeology for Westphalia, said, "This is a first in this form in the western part of the Germanic settlement area. In addition to the first pottery kiln, we found metalworking workshops, which were exceptionally well preserved."What do the furnaces reveal about ancient metalworkingThe excavated furnaces provide details about how the metal was processed. Jan Rosbeck of the Dortmund City Archaeology Department said, "The Germanic tribes melted Roman scrap metal here in crucibles that they placed in kilns. These were round to oval structures with clay walls, into which air was pumped from the sides using bellows to regulate the temperature." These remains provide physical evidence of the facilities used to process Roman metal scrap. The LWL identified them as part of the metalworking area uncovered during the excavation. The structures provide further archaeological evidence of Germanic metalworking during the Roman Imperial Period.More clues remain to be uncovered at the ancient workshopThe excavation is now nearly complete, although some questions about the site remain unanswered. The archaeologists do not yet know what type of pottery was produced in the kiln. The team plans to completely recover the best-preserved furnace so that the unique archaeological remains can be put on display in the future.The excavation began in mid-August and is being carried out by LWL Archaeology for Westphalia together with the Dortmund City Archaeology Department. The workshop area includes the pottery kiln and metalworking facilities, along with pits, furnaces and hearths.Why is the discovery important beyond the regionThe metalworking remains are especially important because they provide evidence for Germanic metal processing outside the Roman Empire. Prof. Dr. Michael Baales of LWL Archaeology for Westphalia said, "It has been known for some time that the Germanic tribes, particularly in the late Imperial period, recycled large quantities of Roman metal objects acquired through trade or plunder."Tobias Zacharias of the Dortmund City Archaeology Department said such work had not previously been documented through archaeological remains. He said the discovery makes the site significant beyond the region and gives the excavation wider archaeological importance.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
