articles.title: Junior Asia Cup winner returns to leaking clay home in Gumla
articles.summary: Junior Asia Cup gold medalist Parwati Topno returns to rain-damaged clay home in Gumla, facing leaks, poor water supply and no housing scheme aid.
articles.body: Gumla: When 18-year-old Parwati Topno returned from China with a Junior Asia Cup hockey gold medal, celebration gave way to heartbreak. At Kumhartoli village in Kamdara block of Gumla, the India junior women’s team player found her family’s clay house damaged by recent heavy rain.The verandah leaks when it rains. The toilet, built years ago, is in a dilapidated condition. Drinking water comes mostly from a village hand pump, as the household connection is irregular and inadequate. Her father, Soma Topno, a mason and sharecropper, has not received any benefit under a housing scheme.Parwati was part of the Indian women’s team that won gold in Moqi this month, defeating hosts China 1-0 in the final. But back home, the medal-winning defender’s family continues to live with cracked walls, leaking shelter and uncertain work.“On returning home, I felt upset seeing my house damaged on account of rain. We have not been allotted any housing scheme so far, while we draw drinking water from the village hand pump. Water supply through the house connection is not regular and sufficient. The toilet built years ago is in a wretched state. My father doesn’t get regular masonry work and works in farmland of others as a sharecropper,” Parwati said.Her elder brother works as a migrant labourer in Karnataka, while her sister stitches clothes in a garment factory in Tamil Nadu.Parwati’s journey began at the day-boarding hockey centre at Glosap Memorial School, Kamdara. In 2018, she cleared a trial and joined the Govt Girls’ School Residential Training Centre, Bariatu in Ranchi. She later played in the Nehru Junior Girls’ Hockey Tournament in Delhi and the Sub-Junior Women’s National Championship in Simdega.After Class 12, she was selected for the Centre of Excellence, Morabadi. She played the Khelo India Youth Games in Chennai and the Junior Women’s National Hockey Tournament in Ranchi in 2024.“In 2025, I was chosen for Khelo India Scholarship and Junior India camp. The same year, I made my international debut in practice matches in Argentina and Germany. In 2025 itself, I was made part of the national team for the Junior World Cup,” Parwati recalled.Stay updated with the latest Ranchi news. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: Trump administration rejects UN pandemic preparedness declaration
articles.summary: The U.S. rejected a nonbinding United Nations declaration pledging international collaboration to improve pandemic preparedness and prevention, joining the European Union in objecting to the parts of the statement. Erica Schwartz, director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), in a speech Friday at a high-level United Nations meeting on pandemic preparedness said the…
articles.body:
The U.S. rejected a nonbinding United Nations declaration pledging international collaboration to improve pandemic preparedness and prevention, joining the European Union in objecting to the parts of the statement.

Erica Schwartz, director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), in a speech Friday at a high-level United Nations meeting on pandemic preparedness said the U.S. had ideological concerns with the document and — despite negotiations — “critical issues remain unresolved.”

“The United States is not in a position to support this text in full,” Schwartz said, citing “the inclusion of divisive ideologies that lack definitional consensus” as well as “references to an unfinished negotiation on pathogen access and benefit sharing.”

Schwartz did not specify the ideologies she was referring to, though a draft of the declaration called for prioritizing “mainstream gender equality into all policies and programs” as well as ensuring “universal access to sexual and reproductive health care services,” which could have been construed to include abortion.

The EU in a statement said there were several elements of the document that “represent explicit red lines,” such as technology transfer and international financing obligations.

The document is not legally binding. While it called for international collaboration, there were no set rules for how countries should prepare and respond to pandemics.

Last year, Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. rejected a U.N. political declaration about combatting chronic disease and promoting mental health because the body was exceeding its “proper role” and the declaration promoted abortion and “radical gender ideology.”

In her speech Friday, Schwartz also urged other countries to follow the U.S.’s lead and ban funding for controversial “gain-of-function” research, which the administration has labeled as dangerous.

“We can advance scientific discovery and medical innovation, while protecting public health and national security, and we encourage all member states to join us in this key initiative,” Schwartz said.

Last summer, the administration banned federal funding for any research that could make a pathogen more virulent; render vaccination against the pathogen ineffective; or make a pathogen easier to transmit to people, animals or plants.

The administration has long blamed such research for the COVID-19 pandemic, asserting that a supercharged virus leaked from a lab in Wuhan, China.

articles.title: Delta flight makes emergency landing due to smoke in cabin
articles.summary: A Boston-bound Delta Air Lines flight from Barcelona made an emergency landing in Portugal after smoke was detected inside the cabin on Sunday. Delta Flight 251 made its stop in at Francisco Sá Carneiro Airport in Porto, Portugal, due to what a Delta spokesperson told The Hill was a mechanical issue. A Delta official said…
articles.body:
A Boston-bound Delta Air Lines flight from Barcelona made an emergency landing in Portugal after smoke was detected inside the cabin on Sunday.

Delta Flight 251 made its stop in at Francisco Sá Carneiro Airport in Porto, Portugal, due to what a Delta spokesperson told The Hill was a mechanical issue. A Delta official said fumes were detected in the cabin and, after landing, Portuguese emergency responders treated passengers.

The plane left Barcelona at 3:15 p.m. and landed in Porto at 5:45 p.m. local time, according to the flight-tracking site Flightradar24 .

Eight passengers were treated on the tarmac, with three others hospitalized for treatment, Portuguese emergency officials told Reuters . The flight had 283 passengers and 13 crew members.

“The flight landed safely, and we apologize to our customers for the delay in their travels as we work to get them to Boston as safely and quickly as possible,” the Delta spokesperson said in a statement.

articles.title: Trump ‘surprised’ 5 men released in UK bomb plotting probe
articles.summary: President Trump said Monday he was “surprised” that British authorities released on bail the five men arrested a day prior in connection with a possible terrorist attack at a U.K. air base operated by the U.S. military. “I would’ve said don’t let them have bail. … I’m surprised that they released them. I wouldn’t have…
articles.body:
President Trump said Monday he was “surprised” that British authorities released on bail the five men arrested a day prior in connection with a possible terrorist attack at a U.K. air base operated by the U.S. military.

“I would’ve said don’t let them have bail. … I’m surprised that they released them. I wouldn’t have done that,” Trump told reporters in the Oval Office.

All five men, identified as British nationals in their 20s from London, were arrested Sunday on explosives and terror charges near RAF Fairford air base in southern England after three vans were spotted outside the military installation.

But British authorities announced Monday the men had been released on bail even as they remain under investigation.

Laurence Taylor, the head of Britain’s counterterrorism police, told reporters that detectives were investigating the incident “from every possible angle, including that this may be actively committed by proxies or individuals, either knowingly or unknowingly, working on behalf of a foreign state.”

He did not say whether investigators had found explosives in any of the three vans and did not take questions.

Trump on Sunday insisted Washington and London had worked together in arresting the suspects, who he said had been “under view for a long time” and intended to do “big damage” to the air base.

On Monday the president repeated those claims that the U.K. worked with the U.S. “very closely” in apprehending the men and that “we know everything about them,” even as British authorities said the suspects were arrested after a farmer called police over suspicious vehicles near the base late Saturday night.

Asked if the incident was connected to Iran, Trump replied, “Might be,” but he declined to elaborate.

Iran has denied its involvement in the incident, releasing a statement through its London Embassy saying it “categorically rejects and strongly condemns the recent unfounded and malicious speculations” around the event.

American B-52 and B-1 bombers have taken off from RAF Fairford for missions to Iran since the U.S. and Israel’s joint war began there in February.

Tehran has repeatedly threatened countries that aid Washington in the conflict, adding to speculation as to whether the country has anything to do with the suspicious activity around Fairford.

All of this comes as Trump has sought an off-ramp to the deeply unpopular Iran war, now in its seventh month with no clear end in sight. The conflict has driven up energy costs, with the Strait of Hormuz, a key waterway for the oil industry, closed amid the fighting.

Trump said Saturday he’s rejected Iran’s recent seven-day proposal to reopen the strait and enter a ceasefire and is considering renewed military strikes against the country after the midterm elections in November.

In the Oval Office, Trump said the U.S. had spoken with Iran through mediators Monday but declined to say what was discussed.
